messages:
Maria Gomez: quick recap — ran 3 apples-to-apples suites comparing fp16 (baseline) vs int8-ggml quant + kernel-fallback change. used the same prompt set, identical decoding params, and explicit stop sequences. replay harness + synthetic batcher both exercised. results are odd: int8 shows ~18% lower p95 in steady batches but a ~12% worse p999 tail on replay runs (see logs).
Maria Gomez: command I used:```
run_bench --model rwd-7b-ggml-int8 --harness replay --prompts prompts/llm_pairset.json --decode "temp=0.2,top_p=0.95" --token-align true --stop-seqs "[\"\n\"]" --out /tmp/run1.log
```
Jae Park: did you force tokenizer alignment for both replay and synthetic? small whitespace differences can move token boundaries and change decode steps. :eyes:
Maria Gomez: yes — replay harness feeds exact token ids from recorded trace, and we normalized synth by running tokenize(prompt) and reconstructing to ensure identical byte offsets. used tools/align_tokens.py with --force-whitespace-normalize.
Oli: curious about KV behaviour — when batcher merged requests did you allow cross-request KV reuse? if int8 uses a different kernel on fallback it might invalidate some reuse paths and cause extra memcpy loops.
Maria Gomez: good call — for apples-to-apples we *disabled* cross-request KV reuse in the replay runs to keep cache state consistent. synthetic runs left cache enabled by default to mimic production. that explains part of the delta.
Priya S: can we add tracepoints for kernel selection decisions? e.g. log lines like `KERNEL_SELECT model=rwd-7b kernel=gemm_fused_int8 path=fast_v2 reason="seq_len>512"` so we can correlate tail spikes with kernel fallbacks. also saw a regression after selector tweak in deploy-2026-02-14.
perf-bot: CI: perf-bench/compare/1938765432 posted — baseline: fp16, candidate: int8-fallback. p95 delta -18.2%, p999 delta +12.4%, cpu-offload memcpy count +1.8x. artifacts: s3://rwd-perf/apples/1938765432/.
Jae Park: proposed follow-ups: 1) run single-shot no-cache baseline (KV disabled) 2) same with KV enabled 3) add kernel-select traces + microprofiles for first 128 tokens. run each 3x and aggregate. can we lock batcher to fixed batch sizes (1,4,8) to remove batching heuristics variance?
Maria Gomez: will do. action items: create controlled-harness config (replay_no-kv.json / replay_with-kv.json / synth_fixedbatch.json), add kernel tracepoint + `tracepoint:on kernel_choice` to prod-sim, and rerun 3x each. I'll upload artifacts to s3 and post dashboards under /perf/apples/1938765432. tagging @eng-runtime for visibility. :thumbsup:
